newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Oct trade deficit widens to $1.57 bln.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Oct trade deficit widens to $1.57 bln.

text.p: South Korea's customs-cleared trade deficit widened to $1.57 billion in October from a shortfall of $207 million a year earlier, provisional figures released from the trade ministry showed on Friday.
The ministry said in a statment FOB exports rose 3.2 percent in October on the year, and CIF imports increased 14.8 percent.
Exports of semiconductors in the month fell 44.4 percent from a year ago to $1.3 billion, while total exports excluding semiconductors rose 15.4 percent to $10.59 billion, it said.
"Unit price for the 16 megbit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips fell 80.2 percent to $10 in October from a year earlier," the statement said.
Improvement in exports was recorded in the auto parts and oil products sectors, which rose 43.4 percent and 33.6 percent, respectively.

The statement said imports of consumer goods rose 15.3 percent in October from a year before, while those of capital goods increased 13 percent. Imports of passenger cars soared 78.2 percent. Cosmetics and alcoholic beverage went up 76.2 percent and 66 percent, respectively.
The country's trade deficit totalled $10.06 billion in 1995, compared with $6.34 billion in 1994, the ministry said.

Letters of credit received by South Korean exporters during the first nine months of this year and the first 20 days of October fell 4.7 percent from a year earlier. Import licences issued in the same period increased 9.2 percent.
